title: U.S. Senate · Tennessee

context.text: This election fills the Class II U.S. Senate seat held by Bill Hagerty (R), who first took office in January 2021. Hagerty advanced unopposed from the August 6, 2026 Republican primary. Marquita Bradshaw won the Democratic primary with 54.7% of the vote, defeating Maria Brewer, Kevin Lee McCants, Civil Miller-Watkins, and Diana Onyejiaka.
As of late September 2026, independent election forecasters (Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, Sabato's Crystal Ball, Decision Desk HQ) all rated the general election Solid/Safe Republican.

candidates.name: Bill Hagerty
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed from the August 6, 2026 Republican primary

summary.text: Bill Hagerty is the incumbent U.S. Senator from Tennessee, seeking re-election to a second term. Before the Senate, he was the U.S. Ambassador to Japan (2017-2019), Tennessee's commissioner of economic development under Governor Bill Haslam, and an economic advisor to President George H.W. Bush and Governor Mitt Romney.

background.text: Born in Gallatin, Tennessee; earned a bachelor's degree (1981) and a law degree (1984) from Vanderbilt University.

Served as Tennessee commissioner of economic development under Governor Bill Haslam, as an economic advisor to President George H.W. Bush and Governor Mitt Romney, and as national finance chairman of the Mitt Romney 2008 presidential campaign.
Was a member of Donald Trump's 2016-2017 presidential transition team, where he oversaw presidential appointments.

record.text: Serves on the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee, chairing its Subcommittee on National Security and International Trade and Finance.
Serves on the Senate Appropriations Committee, chairing its Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government.
Serves on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee as ranking member of its Subcommittee on State Department and USAID Management, International Operations, and Bilateral International Development.

candidates.name: Marquita Bradshaw
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 6, 2026 Democratic primary with 54.7% of the vote

summary.text: Marquita Bradshaw is a community organizer and environmental-justice advocate from Memphis running for U.S. Senate. She is the founder and executive director of Sowing Justice, a nonpartisan civic-engagement organization, and previously was the Democratic nominee for this same Senate seat in 2020.

background.text: An alumna of the University of Memphis, Bradshaw has worked in labor, environmental, education-reform, tax-reform, trade-policy, and social-justice advocacy.
Is the founder and executive director of Sowing Justice, which she describes as a nonpartisan organization focused on civic engagement beyond voting.
Has worked as a caretaker for a differently abled adult and says she experienced medical bankruptcy.

priorities.text: Build an economy that works for working people, including ensuring a living wage and restructuring the tax system to shift the burden of income, sales, and property taxes away from working Americans.
Pursue a transition away from fossil fuels toward renewable energy, framed as reducing energy costs and pollution-driven healthcare burdens.
Expand comprehensive healthcare coverage, including mental, dental, vision, and reproductive health services, and support rural hospitals.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for a 'just transition to a circular economy' focused on renewable energy and says the campaign will pursue 'bold environmental and climate action.'
positions.quote: Break our dependency on fossil with a just transition to a circular economy which focus on clean renewable energy, affordable housing, public transportation, expanding Medicare, and green jobs.

positions.summary: Supports expanding Medicare to address the health burdens of pollution and climate change, and says healthcare legislation must comprehensively cover mental, dental, vision, and reproductive care.
positions.quote: Expanding Medicare for all to mitigate the disproportionate burdens of pollution and climate change.

positions.summary: Calls for restructuring what she describes as a regressive tax system to remove the tax burden from working Americans.
positions.quote: Restructure the regressive tax system to fairly tax all working Americans, removing the burden of income, sales & property taxes from the working population.

positions.summary: Lists ensuring a living wage as part of her economic platform.
Emphasizes quality childcare and wrap-around services for working families, and supports universal pre-K.
positions.quote: Supports universal pre-K education giving children the foundation to be lifelong learners

summary.text: Andrew Gerena is an independent candidate describing himself as a working-class American with a background in military service, commercial trucking, information technology, food service, and scientific research.

background.text: Says he has life and employment experience ranging from military service to security, commercial trucking, information technology, food service, and scientific research.

priorities.text: Lists a series of specific policy positions including repealing Tennessee restrictions on rent price controls, right-to-repair protections for farmers, pro-nuclear energy, repealing the Patriot Act, and ending U.S. involvement in what he calls regime-change wars.

positions.summary: Calls for repealing Tennessee's state-level restrictions on local rent price controls.
positions.quote: Repealing Tennessee's Restrictions against enacting ANY reasonable rent price controls.

summary.text: Robert Jones is an independent candidate who describes himself as a historian, educator, business owner, archaeologist, and nonprofit leader. He says he accepts no campaign donations and created a 'Public Service Pledge' committing to transparency and accountability.

background.text: Describes his background as a historian, educator, business owner, archaeologist, and nonprofit leader.
Says he accepts no campaign donations and has no political party directing his decisions.

priorities.text: Created and signed a 'Public Service Pledge' committing to principles including equal representation, evidence before opinion, transparency, fiscal responsibility, civil discourse, and accountability, along with a proposed 'Accountability Framework' for constituent oversight of his Senate office.

summary.text: James Macon III is an independent candidate who says he is a global business strategist with more than 25 years of Fortune 500 leadership experience, and a former journalist for outlets including CNN.

background.text: Says he is a Senior Director at Stryker with prior executive roles at Medtronic and Wright Medical, and holds an MBA from the University of Tennessee and an MA from Northern Illinois University.
Says his background includes five years as a journalist, including for CNN, and a decade of church leadership as a pastor and educator.

priorities.text: Focuses on lowering costs, creating jobs, and building stronger communities, including advanced manufacturing, infrastructure investment, and workforce training.

summary.text: David Sutman Jr. describes himself as a working-class Tennessean and political outsider running as an independent to focus on cost-of-living issues and government accountability.

background.text: Describes himself as having spent his career 'solving real-world problems' rather than in politics.

priorities.text: Says the federal government should refocus on policies that ease the cost burden on working families, including support for small businesses and economic growth.
Emphasizes government transparency and accountability to constituents over party loyalty.

summary.text: Tharon Chandler is an independent candidate on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot for U.S. Senate. Chandler previously ran as an independent in the 2024 U.S. Senate race in Tennessee.
Jeremy Hearn is an independent candidate on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot for U.S. Senate. No campaign website or public policy statements were found.
Yoshi Matthews is an independent candidate on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot for U.S. Senate. No campaign website or public policy statements were found.
Catherine Whitson is an independent candidate on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot for U.S. Senate. No campaign website or public policy statements were found.

researchNotes: Bill Hagerty did not complete Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey and no accessible press-release archive was found on his official Senate site during this research pass, so his stated 2026 campaign positions are not documented here beyond his committee roles; his federal key votes and FEC totals are added separately by script. Tharon Chandler, Jeremy Hearn, Yoshi Matthews, and Catherine Whitson are independent candidates with no Candidate Connection survey responses or discoverable campaign websites/public statements as of this research pass.
